bull_bear.body:
- Depth of vertical integration - the Company manages spinning, weaving, processing, dyeing, finishing and packing in-house, which it states gives better control over quality, consistency, turnaround time, design responsiveness and cost competitiveness
- Denim scale and category position - capacity built up in steps from 10 MMPA at entry in 2005 to 140 MMPA by 2019, described in the AR as establishing JWL among the leading integrated denim fabric manufacturers
- Portfolio breadth across denim, bottom-weight fabrics, premium shirtings and dyed yarn, which the Company presents as supporting customer diversification and resilience across demand cycles
- Long-standing relationships with leading domestic and international customers, cited as a durable asset built on execution discipline
- Backward integration into spinning (unit commenced 2012 at 45 tonnes per day, raised to 110 tonnes per day under a 2021 investment) supporting raw-material control
- Optionality from diversification - consumer fabric brands RICCORA and LINEN GRAZIA, and an electric two-wheeler platform through Jindal Mobilitric
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Responsible chemical management - dependence on ZDHC / OEKO-TEX / GOTS certification to hold customers — Flagged by the Company as a risk with NEGATIVE financial implications: 'It can have a very large negative impact in terms of loss of business if the CMS is not complied with.' Hazardous chemicals threaten employee and consumer health; various nations restrict or prohibit certain substances and non-compliance can bring legal difficulties and fines, and spills can damage the environment and reputation. Mitigation is a Chemical Management System certified to ZDHC, OEKO-TEX and GOTS and continuously monitored by third-party auditors - which makes certification status a business-continuity dependency, not just a compliance item
- Product quality and safety - a quality escape is framed as a loss-of-business event — Flagged with NEGATIVE financial implications: 'It can have a very large negative impact in terms of loss of business if the safety and quality standards are not met.' Mitigated by process control and quality assurance with 100% inspection of goods before dispatch and stated zero incidents of product recall on safety grounds. Watch item in the same BRSR: customer complaints filed rose to 767 in FY 2025-2026 from 267 in FY 2024-2025, with 13 pending at the close of the year against 20 a year earlier
- Carbon emissions and energy management — Textile production contributes notably to the carbon footprint and the manufacturing process can also release SOx, NOx and other airborne pollutants. Mitigation stated: biomass and other sustainable fuels replacing coal for steam generation, and increasing renewable (solar) energy for scope 1 energy consumption. The Company classifies the financial implication as positive because brands globally favour GHG reduction
- Water availability and wastewater compliance — Water is pivotal to production; water-intensive operations face operational interruption from scarcity, higher procurement cost and capital investment, and process wastewater must be treated before discharge or the Company incurs regulatory-compliance and mitigation cost. Mitigation stated: an installed wastewater recovery facility (the director's ESG statement adds a Zero Liquid Discharge treatment facility)
- Waste management — Waste arises as a by-product of operations, machinery maintenance and administration; inadequate management could cause air pollution, climate impact, ecosystem consequences and health and safety risk. Mitigation: recycling and re-use of process waste and post-industrial waste, which the Company also treats as a commercial opportunity because customers prefer suppliers offering recycled-content fabrics
- Workplace health and safety — Flagged with NEGATIVE financial implications: failure can bring financial penalties and legal consequences, serious incidents can cause severe injuries and liabilities, and safety events cause project delays and downtime that raise cost and reduce profitability. Mitigation: a dedicated safety team, regular training and drills, and monitoring of accident frequency, accident severity rate and accident incident rate by the Head of Safety
- Employee wellbeing and retention — Flagged with NEGATIVE financial implications: a high rate of employee turnover could signal low employee satisfaction to potential investors, while prioritising welfare lowers recruitment and integration cost. The only mitigation stated is safety and skill-upgradation training given to all employees during the year
- Human rights — Flagged with NEGATIVE financial implications: violation can lead to legal consequences, reputational damage and loss of investor confidence. Mitigation: anti-discrimination policy, internal code of conduct and stated procedures
- Corporate governance compliance — Flagged with NEGATIVE financial implications: non-compliance can result in legal and financial penalties. Mitigation: a robust compliance framework and regular audits. No litigation, contingent-liability or auditor-qualification evidence was routed into this bundle, so the severity of this risk cannot be assessed from it

business.body: Jindal Worldwide Limited (JWL), founded in 1986 as a home-textile manufacturer, is an integrated textile enterprise whose portfolio spans denim, bottom-weight fabrics, premium printed shirting fabrics, dyed yarn, value-added fabric solutions, consumer-led brands and electric mobility. Backed by manufacturing facilities in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, it manages key stages of the textile value chain including spinning, weaving, processing, dyeing, finishing and packing, which the Company describes as its principal source of control over quality, turnaround time, design responsiveness and cost competitiveness. Its customers are majorly business organisations from multiple geographies including wholesalers, brands and retailers, served across India and export markets; electric two-wheelers are pursued through subsidiary Jindal Mobilitric.

business.body:
- **Textiles:** Denim fabric, Bottom-weight fabrics, Premium printed shirting fabrics, Dyed yarn, Value-added fabric solutions
- **Consumer-led brands:** RICCORA (in-house fabric brand, launched 2024), LINEN GRAZIA (premium linen brand line)
- **Electric mobility:** Electric two-wheelers (through Jindal Mobilitric)

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the textile core across denim, bottom-weight fabrics, premium shirtings, dyed yarn and value-added fabrics, supported by scale, integration and product depth
- Expand value-added offerings and move beyond commodity fabric positioning by deepening presence in premium shirtings, digitally printed fabrics, specialised finishes and lifestyle-oriented collections
- Build brand-led growth platforms through RICCORA and LINEN GRAZIA to move closer to retailers and end-consumer preferences
- Pursue future-ready diversification into electric mobility through Jindal Mobilitric, building optionality beyond conventional textiles
- Advance design-led and customer-led product innovation through new textures, blends, prints, finishes and performance-oriented fabrics
- Operate with resource discipline - waste reduction, water management, energy optimisation, recycling and safe manufacturing practices - with sustainability-led manufacturing treated as a competitive advantage with global customers
- Deepen customer and market reach through consistent quality, timely delivery and reliable execution across domestic and international markets, including new geographies
- Technology-led execution: strengthen digital print capability, product development systems, data visibility, planning and faster sampling across sales, production and supply chain
- Prudent leadership - the Company states it seeks growth but not at the cost of governance, financial discipline or long-term resilience
- Profit retention over distribution for FY 2025-26. The Board reviewed financial performance and available reserves and, 'in view of conservation of profits for future plans', decided at its meeting held on 25th May 2026 not to recommend any dividend for the financial year; the extract of that paragraph is cut off mid-sentence in this bundle. The Company also did not transfer any amount to the General Reserve for the year ended 31st March 2026. No dividend distribution policy text, payout ratio, buyback, debt-reduction target or credit rating appears in this bundle - the section delivered under the '=== DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY ===' header is in fact Board's Report items 2 to 4 (basis of preparation of financial statements, transfer to reserves, dividend), not the policy itself. On governance mechanics, the Board comprised 6 members as at 31st March 2026 - 2 Non-Executive Non-Independent, 1 Executive (Managing Director) and 3 Non-Executive Independent Directors including 1 woman director - with a Non-Executive Chairman from the promoter category; the AGM notice proposes re-appointment of Mr. Amit Yamunadutt Agarwal as Managing Director for 3 years with effect from 03rd September 2026, and ratification of cost auditor remuneration of Rs. 1,00,000 for FY 2026-2027.
- Shift to sustainable fuels (biomass) for steam generation, replacing coal, described by the Company as a key achievement in reducing greenhouse gas emissions
- Renewable energy expansion through solar panels to reduce scope 1 energy consumption
- Wastewater recovery facility plus a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) water treatment facility enabling treatment and reuse of process water
- Waste management system recycling and reusing both process waste and post-industrial waste, positioned to serve customer demand for recycled-content fabrics
- Chemical Management System certified to ZDHC, OEKO-TEX and GOTS, continuously monitored by third-party auditors
- 100% inspection of goods before dispatch, with zero product recalls on safety grounds stated for the period
- Policies covering all nine NGRBC principles, Board-approved, translated into procedures and published at jindaltextiles.com; value-chain extension of those policies is stated for P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 but NOT for P3, P7, P8 and P9
- Sustainability accountability sits with Mr. Amit Yamunadutt Agrawal, Vice-Chairman and Managing Director, named as the director responsible for sustainability decision-making
- CAVEAT ON TARGETS: the BRSR answers 'Yes' to having specific commitments, goals and targets with defined timelines, but the principle-wise text sets no quantified target or date - for P2, P4 and P6 (environment and stakeholder principles) it states only 'We are taking several initiatives and will conduct formal study and come up with targets', and performance against commitments is recorded as 'NA' for all nine principles
- CAVEAT ON CERTIFICATIONS: BRSR Section B question 4, which asks for national and international codes/certifications/labels/standards adopted and mapped to each principle, is answered '-' for all nine principles, even though the same report's director statement names ZDHC, OEKO-TEX and GOTS
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: This bundle contains no forward capex or expansion plan for FY27 or beyond - no project, no commissioning or ramp timeline and no rupee quantum. What it carries is history and footprint. The 'Our Journey' timeline records past capacity steps: denim entry in 2005 at 10 MMPA, raised to 20 MMPA (2008), 30 MMPA (2010), 50 MMPA (2014), 75 MMPA (2015), 85 MMPA (2016), 116 MMPA (2017) and 140 MMPA (2019); a spinning unit commenced in 2012 at 45 tonnes per day, productivity enhanced by 20 tonnes per day in 2018 and an investment undertaken in 2021 to raise spinning capacity to 110 tonnes per day; bottom-weight fabrics entered in 2014 at 25 MMPA, dyed yarn fabrics in 2015 at 1.1 MMPA and premium shirtings in 2017 at 20 MMPA. Diversification steps recorded are the 2022 acquisition of Earth Energy (electric vehicles) and the 2024 launches of the RICCORA and LINEN GRAZIA fabric brands. On current footprint, the 'JWL in Numbers' at-a-glance page states denim capacity 140 million metres, bottom-weight fabric capacity 30 million metres, premium shirting fabric capacity 30 million metres, dyed yarn capacity 1,550 metric tonnes, 04 manufacturing facilities and a 1400+ workforce - but that page prints no as-of date, its labels and values are separated in the extracted text, and its facility count is not reconcilable with BRSR Section A elsewhere in the report (2 national plants). For that reason those figures are reported here as narrative only and are not carried into installed_capacity. One capex-adjacent disclosure is present and is a nil: BRSR Principle 2 essential indicator 1 reports R&D at 0 and capex at 0 as a percentage of investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, for both FY 2025-2026 and FY 2024-2025, with details recorded as 'NA'.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management describes the FY 2025-26 environment as demanding agility and prudence, shaped by changing consumer preferences, input cost movements, global market shifts, competitive pressures and rising sustainability expectations
- The industry is characterised as shaped by raw material volatility, demand cycles and evolving fashion preferences; the Company says it aims to grow with greater resilience and sharper execution rather than scale alone
- Changing fashion preferences and shorter product cycles are cited as the drivers requiring design-led, digitally printed and application-led fabric development to retain relevance in domestic and international markets
- Global customers increasingly valuing responsible supply chains is presented as making sustainability-led manufacturing a source of business advantage
- India's transition towards cleaner, smarter and technology-led transportation is the stated demand driver for the Jindal Mobilitric electric two-wheeler platform
- Stated FY 2026-27 priorities: strengthen the core textile platform, deepen customer relationships, enhance product innovation, build consumer-facing brands, improve operational efficiency and pursue future-ready opportunities with measured ambition
- NOTE ON EVIDENCE: no demand or margin forecast, no segment-wise performance review and no 'Opportunities and Threats' text is present in this bundle. The section delivered under the '=== MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS ===' header is Board's Report items 26-28, which only state that the MD&A is annexed separately as 'Annexure-E'; the MD&A itself was not routed here.
